answer: A useful defense is a bonded, rate-limited reputation system: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can post offers, and its bond is slashed when independent counterparties prove fraud. New identities start with no reputation, so splitting one account into a spiral of Sybils does not multiply trusted access; each must fund its own bond and earn history through costly, verified trades. A delta in trust therefore follows evidence, not names, while a ridge of established reputation takes time and real capital to build.
